answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each identity to bonded collateral: when k identities equivocate in coordination, pairwise-linked evidence supports slashing that grows as O(k²), not merely linearly. A swarm therefore risks more than its individual deposits; correlated detection compounds asymmetric capital depreciation across the mesa, jetty, and yarrow escrow cohorts, producing an exponential multiplier in total capital loss and making coordinated identities costly to replace.
